items.titulo: Google puts Target and Albertsons grocery carts inside Search and Gemini
items.resumen: Safeway and Shaw's join for US shoppers, while Experian credit checks and H&R Block tax estimates reach Search. Who takes the payment is a question left open.

items.titulo: Amazon's live shopping beta asks brands for 50 Mbps and 1080p video
items.resumen: Select US advertisers stream in Brand Stores with up to 10 products, deals in the first four slots. Reach past the Store leans on paid ads and social posts.

items.titulo: Alibaba and Temu cut marketing as AI engines start handing out coupons
items.resumen: Alibaba and PDD cut marketing spend, AI answers began serving coupon codes before Black Friday, Google raised ad surcharges and AWS moved fraud checks inline.

items.titulo: Brazil's ANPD names 8 platform types presumed to face child safety law
items.resumen: Age checks cannot take an app out of scope, and ad-funded free services count too. What the 69-page guidance means for app stores, AI chatbots and advertisers.

items.titulo: TVP wins top spot in Poland's video rankings with 18.28% share
items.resumen: Polsat fell to 18.06% and Warner Bros. Discovery to 17.93% as YouTube took 34% of its viewing on TV sets. Can a 0.22-point lead outlast the football calendar?

items.titulo: YouTube and Netflix lift Polish streaming to 10.8% of TV time
items.resumen: Other streaming services stayed at 6.6% as Polish viewers added 11 minutes of daily TV in October. Can streaming now pass the 11.0% record it set in August?

items.titulo: OpenAI forces AI model resellers to seek its approval first
items.resumen: Training rival models on its outputs is barred, and apps that only embed its models stay exempt. What counts as an intermediary, and how is approval granted?

items.titulo: Spotify opens a Grand Theft Auto VI music hub in 33 markets
items.resumen: GTA VI's artist page had 29 million monthly listeners before launch, and over 20 radio playlists fill in as fans play. Which 33 markets, and is a brand paying?

items.titulo: Character.ai's $10m bidder faces objection over its unnamed backer
items.resumen: Formed a day before it was chosen, Smirks and Pangs had no named parent or sponsor. The US Trustee wants its $350,000 fee denied. A hearing follows November 23.

items.titulo: Character.ai asks court to keep its $10m buyer's backer secret
items.resumen: New York venture capital fund finances Smirks and Pangs, the filing says, without naming it. A November 23 hearing decides whether users ever learn which one.

items.titulo: Game: Ask five clients what risk means and you get five answers
items.resumen: Sixteen terms in four groups for a calmer Sunday. One set comes from this week's coverage, and the defensive-sounding tiles wander between tiers.

items.titulo: Google teaches AI coding agents to wire Analytics into iOS and Android apps
items.resumen: iOS and Android developers get one skill, firebase-analytics, for setup and screen view logging. Conversion tracking, named in the release note, is not covered.

items.titulo: Shallow pages draw less interest in AI search, Google's Liz Reid says
items.resumen: Preferred sources and creator follows are what Google offers publishers, Reid told a podcast. She gave no traffic figures. Where does AI in the web leave sites?

items.titulo: Twenty ways a programmatic deal goes quiet on Amazon
items.resumen: Deal buyers can read no-bid reasons only 14 days at a time, and results sit in the Inventory report template. Which settings stop ad groups bidding, and why?

items.titulo: Amazon's ad status page still tracks Posts, a feature shut in July 2025
items.resumen: Updated November 20, the help page calls the DSP row DVA+ and lists 19 countries, not Germany. The live page still says Amazon DSP. Which version is current?
Month is an Amazon Ads unified reporting time dimension that groups impressions, spend and sales by calendar month, with up to six years of history retained.
Date range is an Amazon Ads unified reporting time dimension that labels each row with the start and end dates of the period its metrics cover, in all products.
